newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SERVGRO PLANS TWO PHASE UNBUNDLING.
newsitem.headline: SERVGRO PLANS TWO PHASE UNBUNDLING.

text.p: Industrial group Servgro International Ltd said on Tuesday it planned to unbundle the company's assets in two phases which could result in the liquidation and delisting of Servgro during the second half of 1997.

Servgro said the move would unlock shareholder value by eliminating the disount to underlying value at which its shares traded. It will also enable shareholders to obtain direct shareholdings in Nasionale Pers Berpek (Naspers), Forbes Group Ltd and Avis Holdings Ltd.
Servgro said on Monday it would list the Avis car rental concern on the Johannesburg, Namibian and Botswanan stock exchanges in April.

The first phase of the unbundling -- scheduled for April 7, 1997 -- will involve the distribution to shareholders of Servgro's "N" shares in 19.1 percent-held Naspers, shares in 63.7 percent-held Forbes and 85 percent-held Avis.
The record date for the first phase of unbundling is April 4 and Avis shares will be listed on April 7.

As a consequence of the first phase of the unbundling, Servgro shareholders will not receive a final dividend for the year to March 31, 1997. However, they will receive their affected shares cum dividend and will be entitled to dividends declared by Naspers, Forbes and Avis but not yet paid prior to the record date.
